articles.summary: Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jordan Elliott was a surprise inactive for Sunday's game, not traveling with the team. Head coach Robert Saleh told reporters only that Elliott was "dealing with personal stuff." On Tuesday, the Titans released Elliott, along with a cryptic statement referencing an "incident." One never wants to have an incident, but the lack of detail only made the whole thing more mysterious. Later that day, we finally got enough detail to say, Oh yeah, that'll do it . As first reported by Austin Stanley and Easton Freeze of AtoZSports.com and Aaron Wilson of KPRC , last week Elliott got into a practice beef with a teammate and left to go get his gun. Elliott and offensive tackle JC Latham got into a fight during drills at the Titans' facility, the reports say, and Elliott was told by coaches to leave the field. He left the building, going out to the players' parking lot with the intention of retrieving a gun from his car. Defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers, a real hero here, was able to talk Elliott out of getting the gun, and he never brought it back into the building.

articles.author: Chabeli Carrazana
articles.summary: As a nurse in the neonatal intensive care unit, Jean Stone knows what it really means to live in a country with no paid parental leave. She’s watched this scene play out so many times it’s almost the norm: Once their babies stabilize in the NICU, parents often return to work to preserve whatever parental leave they have left for when their babies come home. Stone calls the parents in the middle of the day to update them — starting each call with, “Everything is OK” — and watch them come in at the end of their workday, their faces reflecting the relief of reunion. “They carry that weight of not being there,” Stone, who works at UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital in Pittsburgh, told The 19th. Five months ago, she and the other nurses at Magee, who are in the middle of negotiating a union contract, decided to do something about it. They came together with a coalition of working parents, advocates and some elected leaders to draft a proposal for a paid leave program in Allegheny County. They launched their campaign on Mother’s Day, May 10. articles.summary: About 80 US, Israeli and British volunteers held near Nahalin in West Bank and taken to police station The Israeli military has detained about 80 US, Israeli and British volunteers helping Palestinians harvest olives near Bethlehem, including the New York Democratic congressional nominee Brad Lander, several rabbis and Israel’s former deputy attorney general. “I’ve been detained by the IDF, along with a group of rabbis and volunteers,” Lander posted from a bus taking him to a police station. “We were simply harvesting olives in a grove near Nahalin in the West Bank. The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn’t a crime under any law I know.” Continue reading...
